monetary_policy.label: rate decision
monetary_policy.about: a central bank announcing an interest-rate decision

change_bps.text: the change in the policy rate

new_rate.text: the policy rate (the benchmark rate the bank sets, such as a cash rate, bank rate or target range) after this decision (for a target range, its upper bound)

vote_split.ask: Does the page give the vote as {v}?

economic_data.label: data release
economic_data.definition: a new reading of {indicator}[ of {place}][ for {period}][, published by {publisher}]
economic_data.about: a new reading of an economic statistic being released

notes.timing: The date is the day the data was released, not the period it covers; a period that ended earlier does not make it an earlier event.

actual.text: the newly released reading of {indicator}[ for {place}][, {measure}][ for {period}]

earnings.label: results
earnings.about: a company reporting its financial results for a period

notes.timing: The date is the day the results were reported, not the period they cover; a period that ended earlier does not make it an earlier event.

revenue.text: total revenue (sales, net sales or turnover) of the whole company[ for {period}]

net_income.text: net income (profit, or loss if negative; net income attributable or available to common shareholders counts)[ for {period}]

about.announced: a company agreeing, offering or bidding to buy another company or a stake in it
about.approved: a planned acquisition winning shareholder, court or regulatory approval
about.completed: an acquisition being completed or closed
about.cancelled: a planned acquisition or offer being called off

stage_text: acquiring (agreeing, offering or bidding to acquire, or a later step such as a tender offer result or the closing)
stage_text.announced: agreeing, offering or bidding to acquire
stage_text.completed: completing its acquisition of (has acquired or has bought; an agreement, an approval or a planned closing is not that)
stage_text.cancelled: calling off its planned acquisition of

notes.status: A named bidder's public offer or bid, binding or not, and a deal proposal filed with an exchange or regulator are fact: the offer was made.

deal_value.text: the value of this acquisition (the whole price, not an earn-out or other contingent part alone)

funding.label: funding round
funding.definition: {subject} raising money from investors in a funding round[ ({round})]
funding.about: a private company raising money from investors in a funding round (seed, series A and later, or a strategic investment)

notes.status: A round the company or its lead investor confirms is fact; a report that it is in talks to raise, or seeking money, is not.

amount.text: the amount raised in this round

valuation.text: the company's valuation in this round

lead_investor.ask: Does the page say {v} led the round?

bankruptcy.label: bankruptcy filing
bankruptcy.about: a company entering a court insolvency proceeding (bankruptcy, administration, receivership or liquidation)

notes.event: Any court insolvency proceeding counts: Chapter 7 or 11, insolvency, administration, receivership, liquidation, judicial management or a similar court-supervised restructuring, including the application for it or the appointment of administrators, receivers or judicial managers.

personnel.label: leadership change
personnel.about: a company naming or losing its CEO, CFO, COO, president or chair

notes.event: In a succession, the predecessor's departure counts as news too.

values.chair: chair of the board (chair, chairman or executive chair)

notes.whole: Cuts in one of its own divisions, units or sites are its cuts.

jobs_cut.text: the number of jobs cut or being cut

pct_workforce.text: the share of the whole company's workforce being cut

product_launch.label: product launch
product_launch.about: a company launching or releasing a new product, model, app, chip, device or service

notes.event: The product must be released, made available or formally unveiled by the company; a leak, a teaser or a rumoured launch is not this. Bringing an existing product or service to new places or users, or updating it, is not a launch.

partnership.label: partnership
partnership.definition: {subject} entering a partnership or commercial agreement
partnership.about: companies announcing a partnership, collaboration, joint venture or commercial agreement with each other

counterparties.ask: Does the page name {v} as a party to the agreement?

term.ask: Does the page give the agreement's term as {v}?

security_incident.label: security incident
security_incident.definition: a security incident (breach, hack or cyberattack) at {subject}
security_incident.about: a security incident (breach, hack or cyberattack, including an outage an attack causes) at an organisation

notes.whole: An incident at one of its own businesses, brands, services or sites is its incident, and so is one at a vendor or partner that exposed its own customers' data, or one at a subsidiary that it reports in its own filing or release. So is malware spread through its own marketplace or store, and theft or fraud by its own staff.
notes.status: An incident the affected organisation, its operator or a regulator acknowledges is fact, even when the page also reports what the attackers claim.
notes.timing: The claimed date may be the day it happened or the day it was discovered or disclosed, as the page states.

incident_kind.ask: Does the page describe the incident as {v} (or the same thing in other words)?

records_affected.text: the number of people or records whose data was affected

breakthrough.label: breakthrough
breakthrough.definition: {subject} reporting a new scientific or technical result[ ({kind})]: {result}
breakthrough.about: a company, university, lab or agency reporting a new scientific or technical result: a first, a record or a peer-reviewed finding

notes.event: The organisation, its researchers or a peer-reviewed journal must report the result as achieved. A product going on sale, a goal, a plan, a grant, a result it only expects, or what the work could lead to is not this.
notes.whole: Any institution that led or co-led the work is the party, even when others took part.
notes.status: A result the organisation or a journal reports as achieved or published is fact; an aim, a target, an expected result, a possible use, or a result the page calls possible, tentative or unconfirmed ("may have") is not.

result.ask: Does the page describe the result as {v} (or the same thing in other words)?

journal.ask: Does the page say it was published in {v}?

doi.ask: Does the page give the DOI {v}?

outage.label: outage
outage.about: a major, widespread outage of a company's cloud, internet or platform service

notes.event: The outage must be widespread: a core service failing or unavailable for many customers or users, or for a whole region. Planned maintenance, a problem at a single customer, or a problem limited to one feature, one model, one app platform, a marketing or status site, or delays in a non-core function is not this.
notes.status: An outage the provider acknowledges is fact, and so are widespread failures the page reports as observed from user reports or monitoring.
notes.timing: The claimed date is the day the outage began.

service.ask: Does the page say {v} was affected?

regions.ask: Does the page say {v} was affected?

vulnerability.label: vulnerability
vulnerability.definition: a critical or actively exploited vulnerability[ {cve_id}] in {subject}'s software[ ({product})]
vulnerability.about: a critical (CVSS 9.0 or higher) or actively exploited vulnerability in a vendor's software or hardware being disclosed

notes.event: The vulnerability must be rated critical (CVSS 9.0 or higher) or reported as exploited in the wild; a lower-rated one that is not exploited is not this. Its disclosure, the vendor's advisory or patch, or its listing as known exploited counts.
notes.whole: For this event the vendor whose product has the flaw is the party, not a company attacked through it; for open-source software the project (WordPress, the Linux kernel, OpenSSH) is the vendor.
notes.timing: The claimed date may be the day it was disclosed, patched or listed as exploited, as the page states; an older flaw newly listed as exploited counts on the listing day.

exploited.ask: Does the page say the vulnerability is exploited in the wild?

tech_regulation.label: regulatory action
tech_regulation.definition: an antitrust or regulatory enforcement action against {subject}[ by {regulator}][ ({action})]
tech_regulation.about: a regulator, government or court taking an antitrust or regulatory enforcement action against a technology company: a fine, a lawsuit, a ruling or a settlement

notes.event: The subject must be a technology company (software, internet, platform, hardware, telecom or fintech). A fine imposed, a lawsuit filed by a regulator or government, a court ruling or a settlement counts. An action against a non-technology business or a public body, an investigation opened, a complaint by a rival, a proposed rule, a law being passed or a trade measure against a country is not this.
notes.status: An action the regulator, the court or the company announces is fact; a reported plan to fine or sue is not.

amount.text: the amount of the fine or settlement

infrastructure_investment.label: infrastructure investment
infrastructure_investment.about: a company announcing an investment in a data centre, chip plant or compute facility

notes.event: The company must announce or commit to the investment, with a site or an amount. A reported plan, a site search, a local approval, a funding round or an acquisition is not this.

values.other: a data centre, chip plant or compute facility

capacity_mw.text: the facility's power capacity in megawatts

about.announced: a company announcing or filing plans for an IPO
about.scheduled: a company pricing its IPO or setting its terms or first trading date
about.completed: a company's shares starting to trade after its IPO, or its IPO closing
about.cancelled: a company postponing or withdrawing its IPO

stage_text: listing its shares: the IPO priced or closed or the shares began trading (a filing or plan to go public is not this)
stage_text.announced: announcing or filing plans for an IPO
stage_text.scheduled: pricing its IPO or setting its terms or first trading date
stage_text.completed: listing its shares: the shares began trading or the IPO closed (pricing alone is not this)

shares.text: the number of shares offered in the whole IPO

delisting.label: delisting
delisting.definition: {subject}'s shares being removed from listing[ on {exchange}], or a decision to remove them being announced
delisting.about: a company's shares being removed from an exchange, or that removal being announced

notes.status: A delisting the company or the exchange announces (a decision to delist, a Form 25 filed or to be filed, or a liquidation that ends the listing) is fact.
notes.timing: The date is the day the shares were removed or the decision was announced; an update on an appeal or hearing, or a letter recounting the proceedings, reports an earlier event.

reason.ask: Does the page give the reason as {v} (or the same thing in other words)?

trading_halt.label: trading halt
trading_halt.definition: trading in {subject}'s shares being halted or suspended[ on {exchange}]
trading_halt.about: trading in a company's shares being halted or suspended

notes.event: The page must say trading was halted or suspended; the company asking the exchange to do it is not enough on its own.

reason.ask: Does the page give the reason as {v} (or the same thing in other words)?

resume_time.ask: Does the page say trading resumes at {v}?

match_result.label: result
match_result.about: a match or game finishing, with its final result

notes.event: The match must be over: a half-time or live score, a preview or a schedule is not this.

score.ask: Does the page give {v} as the final score of this match itself (not a series, aggregate, half-time or live score)?

scorers.ask: Does the page say {v} scored in this match?

transfer.label: transfer
transfer.about: a player signing for, joining, being traded to or loaned to another team

notes.status: A move a club, the league or the player confirms is fact; agreed personal terms, a player close to or in talks over a move, or a reporter's word that a deal is done are not.

contract_years.text: the length of {player}'s contract in years

injury.label: injury
injury.definition: {player} being injured or ruled out by an injury[ ({injury})]
injury.about: a player being injured, ruled out or sidelined by an injury, or having surgery

injury.ask: Does the page describe the injury as {v} (or the same thing in other words)?

expected_return.ask: Does the page say {player} is expected back {v}?

award.label: award
award.about: a player, coach or team being given an individual or season award (not a match result or a title won on the field)

election_result.label: election result
election_result.about: an election, referendum or leadership vote being won or decided

notes.status: A result the election authority declares, that the loser concedes, or that a news organisation calls or projects as won is fact; an exit poll, a lead in a partial count, a forecast or a candidate's own claim of victory is not.

about.approved: a legislature or one of its chambers passing a bill
about.completed: a bill becoming law: signed, given assent or promulgated
about.cancelled: a bill being voted down, vetoed or withdrawn

stage_text.completed: becoming law (signed, given assent or promulgated; passing a vote alone is not this)
stage_text.cancelled: being voted down, vetoed or withdrawn

about.announced: a person being named or nominated to public office, or resigning or being removed from it (company officers are leadership changes)
about.approved: a nominee to public office being confirmed
about.completed: a person being sworn in or taking public office
about.cancelled: a nomination to public office being withdrawn or rejected

stage_text: being named to, taking or leaving the office of
stage_text.announced: being named or nominated to, or resigning or being removed from, the office of
stage_text.completed: being sworn in or taking office as
stage_text.cancelled: having a nomination withdrawn or rejected as

about.announced: a government imposing or announcing sanctions, tariffs, export controls or other trade restrictions on a country, company or person
about.completed: sanctions, tariffs or trade restrictions taking effect
about.cancelled: sanctions, tariffs or trade restrictions being lifted, suspended or revoked

stage_text: imposing, putting into effect or lifting

measure.ask: Is the measure {v} (or the same thing in other words)?
